$comment: vacuous-check policy — the ratchet + allowlist contract for scripts/gate_vacuous_check.py
a per-entry `reason` + `owner`, and — critically — a MISSING policy file is NOT
'no policy configured, skip'. The gate treats absence as {mode: "fail", allowlist: []},
the strictest posture there is. Only editing THIS file down to mode:"fail" (or an empty
allowlist) retires an entry; deleting the file cannot silence the gate.
mode:"ramp"  — allowlist entries below suppress their named finding. New violations not
mode:"fail"  — the allowlist is INERT regardless of its contents; every finding fails.
Flipping to this is how an entry is proven fully retired.
Both entries below are pre-existing, already-documented ramps discovered when this gate
landed (2026-08-23) — not new debt this gate introduced. Fixing either for real is out of
devops-engineer's CI-wiring scope: gate-pagination needs contract-designer's pagination
annotations (governance/pagination-standard.md §5), and the AuthN boundary smoke needs the
AuthN provider deploy it is gated on (contract PR #243). Flipping either to enforcing here
would break CI for work this PR did not do.

allowlist.reason: Pre-existing, already-documented report-only ramp (see the job's own comment: "Report-only first pass; ratchet to enforcing per repo once the billing-service contract annotates/allowlists its collection GETs"). governance/pagination-standard.md §5 names contract-designer as the owner of the annotation work that unblocks flipping this to enforcing; not a devops-engineer CI-wiring task.

Explicitly time-boxed by the step's own comment (contract PR #243): the AuthN provider-boundary tests self-skip pre-deploy (gated on /api/v1/security/methods == 200), and continue-on-error exists precisely so a pre-deploy run does not turn the job red. The comment states the retirement trigger directly: "After the deploy, dispatch with run_authn_boundary=true to make it the AuthN gate" — remove continue-on-error at that point, not before.
allowlist.owner: backend-engineer / AuthN deploy owner (tracked by izzywdev)
